extracted.intended_audience: general readers, researchers, and students interested in film censorship and lists of films banned by country
extracted.subtask_description: A country-by-country listing of films that have been censored, restricted, or banned, with the stated reasons given by governments or censorship boards (e.g., violence, sexual content, political subversion, religious offence, national security).

rubrics_metrics.name: graphic violence and nudity
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned due to graphic violence and nudity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples on the page: Salò, or the 120 Days of Sodom (banned for graphic violence and nudity); multiple entries note bans for "high gore violence and cruelty" (e.g., The Texas Chain Saw Massacre; Tenebre). Notes include that some bans were later lifted or re-releases appeared in cut/uncut forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: incest, murder, and rape
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned for dealing with issues of incest, murder, and rape.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Aksharaya (Letter of Fire) was banned for dealing with incest, murder, and rape.

rubrics_metrics.name: religiously sensitive themes / blasphemy / offensive to religious groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned because the film contains material judged to be religiously sensitive, blasphemous, or offensive to a faith.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: The Da Vinci Code (banned for religiously sensitive themes); The Last Temptation of Christ (banned for blasphemic themes); Noah (banned in some markets for depicting the prophets). Vatican City noted The Da Vinci Code as 'inaccurate and offensive to Christians.'

rubrics_metrics.name: extreme violence / high gore / torture
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned for extreme violence, graphic gore, or depictions of torture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: The Exterminator (rated S for extreme violence), Saw VI (banned or restricted due to violent content), Human Centipede II (classification issues and refusal in some places). Some bans are specifically for 'brutal gory violence and torture' (Saw VI in Ukraine).

rubrics_metrics.name: sexual content / explicit erotic scenes
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned or refused classification because of explicit sexual content or erotic scenes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Fifty Shades of Grey (banned in some countries for sexual content); Love (Taiwan) — distributor cut 170 seconds of close-ups on physical intimacy including intercourse, fingering, ejaculation, fellatio before release; many bans involve demands for cuts to obtain ratings.

rubrics_metrics.name: sexually violent content / necrophilia / extreme sexual violence
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned for containing sexually violent content, including necrophilia or scenes of sexualized violence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: A Serbian Film (banned due to extreme/sexually violent content); Necro Lesbians (Nekrology) banned for necrophilia and rape.

rubrics_metrics.name: disrespectful or insulting portrayal of national figures / monarchy
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned because the film could be construed as disrespectful towards a country's monarch or national leaders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: The King and I and Anna and the King were banned in Thailand because they could be construed as disrespectful towards the King of Thailand.

rubrics_metrics.name: negative portrayal of country, institutions, or judicial system
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned for portraying the country, its institutions, court system, or society negatively or as corrupt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Brokedown Palace banned in Thailand for negative portrayal of Thailand and its judicial system; The Route (Tanzania) was banned as it 'showed too much sex and nudity' and was labelled a 'threat to Tanzanian culture'; Hunter Killer (Ukraine) banned for demonstrating 'the military power of Russia' (i.e., national-security/political sensitivities).

rubrics_metrics.name: appearance of or association with Israeli actors / perceived Israeli ties
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned because the film features Israeli actors or is perceived to have ties to Israel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Ben-Hur was banned in some Arab League states because actress Haya Harareet was Israeli; Wonder Woman and Death on the Nile faced bans for featuring Israeli actress Gal Gadot. In some cases distributors or governments explicitly cite the actor's nationality or actions as the reason.

rubrics_metrics.name: homosexual themes / depiction of homosexuality
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned because the film depicts homosexual themes or LGBT content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Brokeback Mountain was banned in the UAE for depicting homosexual themes; Brüno was banned in Ukraine for homosexual themes. LGBT content is repeatedly cited as grounds for bans in multiple jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: child sexualization / exploitation imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned for imagery considered to sexualize or exploit children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Cuties was banned in some territories (noted here under Turkey/Thailand context in the chunk) because of imagery displaying child sexualization and exploitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: pornography or obscene material
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned on grounds the film is pornographic or obscene.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: I Am Curious (Yellow) was banned because of pornography; some films initially banned were later allowed after court cases or cuts (I Am Curious (Yellow) allowed after court case).

rubrics_metrics.name: political subversion / criticism of regime / satire of government
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned because the film is judged subversive, criticizes the regime, satirizes bureaucracy, or otherwise threatens political authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Ciguli Miguli and W.R.: Mysteries of the Organism were banned under Josip Broz Tito's regime for political satire; The Dictator banned in Tajikistan for subversiveness; many entries note bans during authoritarian regimes for political content.

rubrics_metrics.name: depictions of territorial disputes / sensitive maps (e.g., nine-dash line)
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned for showing maps or imagery that assert disputed territorial claims or other geopolitically sensitive content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Abominable, Uncharted, and Barbie were banned in Vietnam for showing the nine-dash line; distributors sometimes argue content was incidental but authorities treat it as politically sensitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: presence or support of blacklisted/controversial individuals (e.g., visiting occupied territory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned because a cast or crew member has engaged in actions that led to blacklisting (e.g., visits to disputed/occupied territories).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: John Wick: Chapter 4 and Machete faced bans or unofficial bans because co-stars (Donnie Yen, Steven Seagal) were associated with visits to Crimea or other politically sensitive actions; 8 First Dates was affected by an actress blacklisted for visiting Crimea.

rubrics_metrics.name: incitement of hate or content judged to incite violence/hate
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned for allegedly inciting hatred or for being judged to incite hate against groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Chavismo: The Plague of the 21st Century was banned from public and university screenings for supposedly inciting hate; some documentary bans cite 'inciting hate' or 'incitement' as the legal basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: instructional sexual content / potential to be imitated by minors
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned because the film shows how to perform sexual acts or produce pornography, raising concerns minors might imitate it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Zack and Miri Make a Porno was banned by a ministry in Thailand because it depicted characters making their own pornographic video and officials worried teens may try to mimic this behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: conflict with cultural values / 'too westernised' portrayals
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned or refused clearance because the film conflicts with local cultural values or is judged 'too westernised' in its depiction of social issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Sex and the City 2 was banned in Vietnam for conflict of 'cultural values'; Xich lo (Cyclo) was banned in Vietnam for being 'too westernised' in its portrayal of urban poverty.

rubrics_metrics.name: portrayal of certain organizations or movements (e.g., banned insurgent groups)
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned because the film depicts banned organizations, insurgent movements, or groups sensitive to the state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Cambodian bans include films portraying the Tamil Tigers or other groups that governments judge harmful to reputation or security; governments sometimes block broadcast or public showing for this reason.

rubrics_metrics.name: accuracy concerns / deemed inaccurate and offensive to a group
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned because authorities deem the film inaccurate or offensive to a particular group (often religious or national).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: The Da Vinci Code was noted as being banned (Vatican City) because it was deemed 'inaccurate and offensive to Christians'; other bans cite 'inaccuracy' alongside offence as a justification.
